what_it_does: Academic chip design typically requires multi-year development cycles and expensive iterations. This work tackles the problem of enabling university researchers to design and fabricate modern chips within a single semester using Intel 16 technology (a 7nm-equivalent process). The team built infrastructure and automated workflows for design, optimization, and place-and-route (the step that physically arranges millions of transistors on silicon) to dramatically compress the timeline. They demonstrated the approach by completing multiple full chip tapeouts (sending designs to fabrication) in one semester, making state-of-the-art hardware research much more accessible to academics.
